algorithm.aligned_dispatch: when the plain test fails and tzcnt(alignment) != 0: reallocation calls the slot 0x64df580 entry 0x635a790 with (old pointer, byte size, tzcnt(alignment)); fresh allocation calls the slot 0x64df590 entry 0x63577f0 with (byte size, tzcnt(alignment))
algorithm.failure_publication: allocator returned null: tag 1 at +0x00, the alignment argument at +0x08, the byte size at +0x10; callers hand (+0x08, +0x10) to the shared failure entry, so the failure pair is (alignment, byte size) on this path and (0, unwritten) on the guard path
algorithm.guard: byte size = count * width: the full product is formed by one unsigned mul; failure when the product overflows 64 bits (mul overflow flag) OR the low 64 bits exceed (2^63 - alignment) mod 2^64, unsigned; on failure the routine writes tag 1 at +0x00 and 0 at +0x08, leaves +0x10 unwritten, and calls nothing
algorithm.plain_dispatch: plain form when (alignment < 0x11 and alignment <= byte size) or tzcnt(alignment) == 0 (exactly alignment == 1): reallocation calls the slot 0x64df588 entry 0x635a7a0 with (old pointer, byte size); fresh allocation calls the slot 0x64df480 entry 0x6355830 with (byte size)
algorithm.success_publication: allocator returned non-null R: tag 0 at +0x00, R at +0x08, the byte size at +0x10
algorithm.zero_size: old size == 0 and byte size == 0: no allocator call; result is tag 0, the alignment argument at +0x08, 0 at +0x10

consumers.argument_order: at the inspected sites the count is passed in rcx and the element width in r9 (growth routine 0x5963a6f, ring stub 0x5962d55, stub family); the boundary multiplies rcx by r9, so the factor roles are the caller's convention, not read from the body
consumers.failure_consumption: callers compare the dword at out+0x00 with 1; on failure they call the shared failure entry 0x141e264 through GOT slot 0x64df498 with (out word +0x08, out word +0x10)
consumers.growth_routine_site: 0x5963a6f, inside the buffer growth routine 0x5963a10 (RE-001-buffer-grow-963a10-115, PR #3346): (out = stack slot, old capacity in elements, old data pointer, computed new capacity, forwarded word as alignment, element size)
consumers.inspected_fresh_site: 0x50de490 (FDE 0x50de300..0x50de518, the RE-012 curl body helper's owner): passes (out, 0, 1, 8, 1, 1) - old size 0 selects the fresh family, the old-pointer word 1 is never read on that path, byte size 8, alignment 1
consumers.inspected_stub_family: a row of near-identical per-type growth stubs (e.g. FDE 0x5962d20..0x5962d84 with element width 0x40, FDE at 0x59635e0 with width 0x1b0) passes alignment 8, its element width in r9 and the computed new capacity in rcx; the success arm stores the +0x08 word as the new data pointer and keeps its own count register as the new capacity

object_layout.inputs: rdi = out (24-byte result struct), rsi = old size as the caller counts it (read only for zero/non-zero), rdx = old data pointer (forwarded verbatim to the reallocation callees; never dereferenced, never null-tested), rcx = element count, r8 = alignment, r9 = element width in bytes
object_layout.result_struct: +0x00 tag qword (0 success, 1 failure; callers compare the low dword with 1), +0x08 on success the new data pointer / on failure the alignment argument (0 after the guard), +0x10 the requested byte size (unwritten on the guard path only); rax at the return is the leftover store offset (8 after the guard failure, 0x10 otherwise), not a result channel

routines.inputs: rdi = out (24-byte result struct), rsi = old size (zero/non-zero only), rdx = old data pointer, rcx = element count, r8 = alignment, r9 = element width
routines.name: allocation boundary (size guard, alignment dispatch, result publication)
routines.outputs: the 24-byte result struct at rdi: tag at +0x00, pointer-or-alignment at +0x08, byte size at +0x10 (guard path leaves +0x10 unwritten); no value return channel is used by callers

unknowns: The four allocator callees' internals (entries 0x6355830, 0x63577f0, 0x635a7a0 and the 0x635a790 prologue into 0x6350210): how each allocates or moves storage, and whether the aligned forms interpret the trailing-zero count exactly as log2 of a power-of-two alignment for every input the dispatch can produce (including non-power-of-two alignments such as 0x18, whose tzcnt is 3). Their call contracts and result convention (pointer or null in rax) are pinned; their bodies are separate questions.

What the alignment argument denotes for callers that forward it opaquely: the buffer growth routine's forwarded word reaches this routine's alignment slot unchanged (see the growth packet), and at the byte-wise sites inspected there it equals 1; this body only requires it to behave as the guard limit's subtrahend and the dispatch's tested value.

Whether any caller can pass a non-zero old size with a stale or null old pointer: the boundary forwards the pointer word to the reallocation callees untested, so that combination is a caller-contract question, not observable here.

The shared failure entry 0x141e264's onward behaviour with the two failure pairs this routine produces ((0, unwritten) after the guard, (alignment, byte size) after a null return): its rdi==0 dispatch is recorded by the growth packet; neither onward target is followed here.
unwind: the routine's FDE (offset 0x3144c4, length 0x34) references CIE 0, whose augmentation is 'zR' (no 'L', no personality), and the FDE's own augmentation length is 0: the routine has no LSDA and no landing pads, so a raise out of an allocator callee runs no cleanup in this frame
